winner.title: Lamb Mafé (Senegalese Peanut Stew)

evidence.authenticity: Written by a Senegalese-born chef who learned it from her mother; gives the Senegalese name (mafé yapp) and context; classic base of onion, pepper, celery, tomato paste, okra thickener, peanuts blended with cooking liquid, rice. Senegalese rather than Malian variant, which is allowed as a regional variant.
evidence.precision: Volumes and cut sizes (2-inch lamb cubes, 3 lb, 8 cups stock); no grams. Doneness cues for lamb sear (golden), tomato paste (darkens, sticks to pot), lamb (pulls apart with a fork), sauce (red oil rises after resting). Pan size only 'large heavy pot'. No Recipe schema, so read via WebFetch.
evidence.testing: Author explains why for searing, tomato-paste browning, dawadawa umami, okra as thickener, and peanut vs peanut butter. Saveur editorial. No test-kitchen claims.
evidence.photos: One finished-dish photo only; no step photos.
evidence.efficiency: 3.5 hours total, mostly braise time for lamb; 30-minute rest is a real step. Reasonable for the dish but long.
evidence.access: Dawadawa is hard to find, but balsamic vinegar is given as a substitute. Natural peanut butter accepted for roasted peanuts. Lamb leg, okra and habanero are available in US stores.

winner.why: It is the only candidate with an authentic author, specific doneness cues and explained technique, while the Malian-named Foreign Fork version has fewer cues and no author expertise.

runnerUp.title: West African Peanut Stew (Tigadegue-Na or Maafe)

evidence.authenticity: Names the Malian tigadegue-na and uses a tomato and peanut butter base with beef and root vegetables; author is not from Mali and the recipe is a simplified home version.
evidence.precision: Only 2 of 14 ingredients have weights; cues are 'until brown', 'vegetables cooked', and 'oil renders on top'. No pan size.
evidence.testing: Little reasoning given beyond a note on the oil rendering as the doneness sign.
evidence.photos: 32 images on the page, but none in the schema steps and not confirmed as process photos.
evidence.efficiency: 110 minutes; the final 30-minute uncovered simmer is a sensible reduction.
evidence.access: All ingredients are at a US grocery.

runnerUp.why: Less precise and less well explained than the Saveur recipe, though it is closer to the Malian name and is faster.
